OpenAI Private Market Note (OPAIPon) is now live as collateral.

In a landmark first, tokenized exposure to OpenAI is now usable as collateral on the same platform as pre-IPO OpenAI perps.

This unlocks a new basis trade: Hold spot OPAIPon for tokenized OpenAI exposure, post it as collateral, and short the OPENAI perp.

When the OPENAI perp trades at a premium to OPAIPon, this basis trade aims to capture that gap as the two prices converge. Holding spot and shorting the perp can capture that convergence if spot rises toward the perp, the perp falls toward spot, or both. Traders can also earn funding payments when rates are positive.

Using OPAIPon as collateral also makes hedging more capital efficient. Traders can hold tokenized OpenAI exposure and use those same holdings to contribute margin for a short OPENAI perp, reducing the need for additional stablecoin collateral.

Arunachal Pradesh deserves more attention than a viral border clip.

On October 22, ITBP chief Shatrujeet Kapur acknowledged that face-offs with Chinese troops were continuing at multiple locations. That deserves clear public updates, especially when unverified invasion videos are circulating alongside actual reporting.

Meanwhile, the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project has triggered protests over ancestral land, displacement and the river’s future. Reports of women injured during confrontations and arrests of activists should put meaningful dialogue at the centre of the response.

India’s concern about China’s upstream dam is understandable. But calling a project strategically important doesn’t settle the questions of the people who would live with its consequences.

There’s another Arunachal story here too: kiwis reaching Dubai markets, and Tawang welcoming tourism delegates. People are building livelihoods while their state gets reduced to a flashpoint.

Defend the border, explain the dam, listen to residents. Those responsibilities belong together. The people of Arunachal should be central to decisions about Arunachal.

🚨 these 3 github repos are the most POWERFUL trading combo i've ever seen

Hedge funds pay analysts, traders and risk teams millions a year. These 3 repos turn that whole team into AI agents you can run for free

It's TradingAgents, ai-hedge-fund and freqtrade, with 238k+ stars combined.

First, get how it works:

1. TradingAgents is a multi-agent framework that mirrors the dynamics of real-world trading firms: fundamental, sentiment, news and technical analysts write reports, bull and bear researchers debate them, a trader decides and a risk team signs off.

2. ai-hedge-fund is a proof of concept for an AI-powered hedge fund: agents modeled on investors like Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Michael Burry and Cathie Wood each give a signal, then a risk manager and a portfolio manager make the call.

3. freqtrade is the free, open source trading bot that turns a signal into a strategy, with backtesting, hyperopt and a dry-run mode that trades on paper first.

Here's how you can run it for free yourself:

1. Open Claude Code and clone the 3 repos: TradingAgents, ai-hedge-fund and freqtrade

2. Run TradingAgents' CLI with python -m cli.main and pick a ticker

3. Watch the analyst team write its reports, the bull and bear researchers argue, and the trader and risk team land on BUY, SELL or HOLD

4. Install ai-hedge-fund with pipx install aihf and run it on the same tickers. Every investor agent returns a signal and a confidence

5. Have Claude merge both: only act when TradingAgents and the investor agents agree

6. Have Claude turn that merged signal into a freqtrade strategy

7. Backtest it in freqtrade on 2 years of data, fees included

8. Tune it with freqtrade hyperopt, then re-test on data it never saw so you don't fool yourself with overfitting

9. Run it in dry-run mode for 2 weeks. If it doesn't beat buy-and-hold after fees, it's not an edge yet

At a gas station, Jensen Huang was asked for his ZIP code and couldn’t answer. The Nvidia CEO says he doesn’t even know his own address.

The conversation began with the skills children are losing. “Try to try to get a kid to do long division right now.” Huang said multiplication tables, square roots and other basic math were being forgotten, then asked whether it mattered.

“Yeah, I don't think it does.” He argued that people may discover new skills that matter instead.

Then Huang offered a personal example. “I actually don't know my address.” Someone pushed back, but he insisted it was true, saying Janine and Lori could confirm it.

He recalled stopping to pump gas a few years earlier, when he was asked for his ZIP code. “And I panicked. I didn't know my zip code.” He added that he forgets his telephone number too, and can live with it.

In the video below, Huang explains why he thinks forgetting these everyday facts may not matter, even as he recounts being stumped at the pump.

Is forgetting basic facts harmless if we can still function without them?

This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
